_readme: Registry of the texture masks. 'kind' is 'patent-drawing' only when the mask comes straight from a patent's own drawing; 'adapted' means the drawing was redrawn by an AI image model and its edges repaired so it tiles. Never describe an 'adapted' pattern as the patent's drawing. 'url' is the Google Patents page (null if unknown; cite by number). 'credit' is the ready-to-paste attribution line shown in the studio. 'procedural' entries are generated SVG-noise tiles from masks/low-pile-carpet.css (read by tools/build_studio.py via 'cssVar'); they have no patent and need no credit. 'defaultSize' is the tile width in CSS px (default 520). inventor/granted are null for procedural entries (no patent).

patterns.title: Crowe carpet, 1884
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)
patterns.note: Genuine drawing, deskewed 0.5 degrees and cropped to a repeat that wraps both ways. The drawing shows two horizontal repeats, used together. Fine horizontal dashes are scan artifacts of the original engraving. Compared with the patent sheet (PDF read): same motifs, two repeats side by side.
patterns.credit: Background pattern from US Design Patent No. 14,685 (Eugene A. Crowe, 1884); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: Crowe carpet, 1882 (medallions)
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)
patterns.note: The patent drawing is a single swatch that does not tile. Redrawn with an AI image model, then edges repaired with make_tileable.py. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 12,657 (Eugene A. Crowe, 1882); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: Crowe carpet, 1882 (leaf bouquet and frames)
patterns.note: Swatch redrawn with an AI image model, edges repaired. The central bouquet is partly re-cut by the repair. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 13,102 (Eugene A. Crowe, 1882); the patent has long expired.
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)

patterns.title: Crowe carpet, 1882 (dense foliage)
patterns.note: Swatch redrawn with an AI image model, edges repaired. Densest pattern in the set; keep opacity low. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 13,483 (Eugene A. Crowe, 1882); the patent has long expired.
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)

patterns.title: Crowe carpet, 1882 (patchwork)
patterns.note: Swatch redrawn with an AI image model, edges repaired. Its fine grid can blur when shown smaller than about 400 px. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 13,105 (Eugene A. Crowe, 1882); the patent has long expired.
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)

patterns.title: Crowe carpet, 1882 (wildflowers)
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)
patterns.note: Swatch redrawn with an AI image model (Google Gemini), then edges repaired with make_tileable.py. Five-petal flowers, leaf sprays and cloud shapes on a brick-like grid. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 13,106 (Eugene A. Crowe, 1882); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: E. Fisher carpet, 1882 (ferns and stepped block)
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)
patterns.note: Swatch redrawn with an AI image model (Google Gemini), then edges repaired with make_tileable.py. Dense fern and leaf foliage over a fine square grid, with one stepped geometric block motif. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs. Dark and busy, so keep strength low behind text. Inventor is Edwin Fisher, not Crowe.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 13,108 (Edwin Fisher, 1882); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: E. Fisher carpet, 1882 (blooms on fine grid)
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)
patterns.note: Swatch redrawn with an AI image model (Google Gemini), then edges repaired with make_tileable_grid.py so the fine square grid lines meet at the join. Dark flowers, tulip-like blooms and a fan-shaped plant on thin stems over a dense grid of dotted cells and dashed hatching. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs. Dark and busy, so keep strength low behind text.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 13,109 (Edwin Fisher, 1882); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: J. Fisher carpet, 1882 (medallion on trellis)
patterns.assignee: Lowell Manufacturing Company (per the patent specification)
patterns.note: Swatch redrawn with an AI image model (Google Gemini), then edges repaired with make_tileable_grid.py so the fine square grid lines meet at the join. Scalloped dark medallions (four corner pieces join into one whole medallion when repeated), a central leaf cluster, small floral sprigs, stepped border motifs, and diagonal lattice and stippled fills over a fine grid. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs. The inventor is John Fisher of New York, not Edwin Fisher of Boston. Very dark and busy, so keep strength low behind text.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 13,110 (John Fisher, 1882); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: H. S. Day textile, 1927 (ogee damask)
patterns.assignee: Pennsylvania Textile Mills, Inc., of Clifton, New Jersey (per the patent specification)
patterns.note: A textile fabric design, not a carpet. Large ogee damask: a dark central medallion with a tulip crown, paisley-shaped panels with cross-hatched fills, scrolls and leafy sprays, on a ground of fine horizontal ruling. Redrawn with an AI image model (Google Gemini), then edges repaired with make_tileable.py. Compared with the patent sheet: same motifs. Known flaw: the Gemini tile had two straight vertical cuts where strips look pasted (about 24% and 76% of its width). The edge repair does not remove them, so faint straight vertical lines show in a repeated view. Re-running Gemini may give a cleaner tile. Dark and busy, so keep strength low behind text.
patterns.credit: Background pattern adapted from US Design Patent No. 74,141 (Harry S. Day, 1927); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: Comp III
patterns.note: The tread design of the Tioga Comp III tire (US D 268,339, expired 1997-03-22). Line art cropped from the patent drawing to a repeat that wraps both ways (3 columns by one vertical repeat; the half-plates cut by the drawing frame join into whole plates). Thin outlines, so it needs more strength than the filled patterns.
patterns.credit: Background pattern from US Design Patent No. 268,339 (Syoji Inae and Eiji Fukuchi, Mitsuboshi Belting Ltd., 1983); the patent has long expired.

patterns.title: Low-pile carpet (procedural)
patterns.note: Generated fine pile noise with a faint 4 px weave, from masks/low-pile-carpet.css. Small-scale, so it pairs with a large pattern without moire. Works best at 6-10% strength.

patterns.title: Pile grain (procedural)
patterns.note: Generated fine pile noise without the weave, from masks/low-pile-carpet.css. Paper or felt grain. Works best at 12-18% strength.
